attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, which he endorses.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'incapable of solving', the claim that this applies to every developer, and the 'most business customers' scope. Treating it as causal fits, since the statement links hallucination to business rejection. The language is firm, with no hedge.

contract.note: The plain reading (practical reliability, more than half of business customers rejecting adoption because of hallucination) is an ordinary, fair reading. But what 'solving' means and which population counts are left undefined, so the evaluator's interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: A peer-reviewed 2024 paper finds that mitigation has only partly worked. That does not show the problem cannot be solved, and it does not measure business rejection.
Survey headlines on business experimentation and risk concerns. No methods were retrieved, and the survey does not attribute non-adoption to hallucination.

reviews.rationale: No evidence in the packet shows a general solution or a general impossibility. No representative study shows whether hallucinations cause most business customers to reject adoption. Neither part of the claim can be settled from this packet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. Only the promise of the rollout is attributed to Altman.

semantics.note: 'Will only increase its cash burn' is firm, so this is a scorable conditional forecast. The antecedent (access for both Plus and free users) is kept. No horizon was stated, and the drafter added none.

contract.note: Reading the claim as incremental net cash burn compared with no rollout is fair: 'only increase' implies no offsetting benefit. Counting the lightweight version is reasonable, because the statement does not tie the claim to a specific model.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own dated announcement of Plus access (Feb 2025) and free access (Apr 2025). It establishes the antecedent, not the outcome.
OpenAI's status page confirms free-user access by Apr 28, 2025. This is evidence of the antecedent only.
Unverified company-wide cash burn for H1 2025. Nothing in it is attributed to the Deep Research rollout.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent was met in April 2025. No evidence isolates the rollout's incremental net cash effect, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Aggregate cash burn cannot settle the forecast.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'Can't raise prices above breakeven' is a firm causal claim about pricing power. The consequence about affordability is hedged with 'likely' and is not scored. The drafter kept that hedge.

contract.note: Reading breakeven as full-cost is the evaluator's choice. The speaker never defined breakeven (inference, product or company-wide), so the result depends on that interpretation. The contract acknowledges this.

evidence.note: A secondary report, citing The Information, of a 70% compute margin by October 2025. Compute margin is not full-cost breakeven, and the report shows no price increase with retained demand. OpenAI did not confirm it.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no product-level record linking price, full cost and retained demand, and nothing isolates utility or differentiation as the cause. The rising compute margin is suggestive context but runs on a different metric. The hedged consequence is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own stated belief in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'I believe' asserts a view without grading confidence, so the claim is treated as firm. 'Turning against' is a fair paraphrase of 'radicalizing', and the 'millions' scale and the Apple Intelligence mechanism are kept.

contract.note: An attitude shift caused by product defects, affecting at least two million people by the post date, is an ordinary and fair reading of the claim.

evidence.note: A survey from Nov–Dec 2024 finds low perceived value of Apple Intelligence. It does not measure any change in general attitudes toward generative AI caused by Apple's features.
A January 2025 report documents faulty notification summaries and Apple's response. It is evidence of the defects, not of a large-scale attitude shift.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows real defects and low perceived value. No representative causal or longitudinal evidence shows that Apple Intelligence turned millions against generative AI, and none rules it out.
